options: A system container and virtual machine manager
questions.answer: A system container and virtual machine manager
questions.explanation: LXD is a system container and virtual machine manager that provides a unified experience for running full Linux systems.

questions.prompt: Which command do you use for day-to-day instance management (create, start, stop)?
questions.explanation: lxc is the client CLI. lxd is the daemon — you use lxd init for setup but lxc for everything else.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between a LXD system container and a LXD virtual machine?
options: Containers use Docker images; VMs use QCOW2
Containers share the host kernel; VMs have their own kernel
Containers are for development; VMs are for production
Containers can only run Ubuntu; VMs can run any OS
questions.answer: Containers share the host kernel; VMs have their own kernel
questions.explanation: System containers share the host kernel (lighter, faster), while VMs boot their own kernel via KVM (stronger isolation).

questions.prompt: Select all that are LXD concepts:
questions.explanation: Instance, Image, Profile, and Storage pool are all core LXD concepts. Pod and Deployment are Kubernetes concepts.
